chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abd al-Rahman al-Hashimi, who said:

He (peace be upon him) said to one of his slaves: 'Buy less for us from the onions, and more for us from the aubergines.' So he said to him (peace be upon him) inquiring, 'The aubergines?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, the aubergines, it gathers all tastes, removes illness, is suitable for the constitution, balanced in its states, suitable for the old man and the young man, moderate in its heat and coldness, hot in the place of heat and cold in the place of cold.'
ai.seo_question: What are the health benefits and characteristics of aubergines according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the Imam (peace be upon him) demonstrates the Shia emphasis on *Tibb al-Nabawi* (Prophetic medicine) by evaluating food through the lens of humoral balance (*Mizaj*). He praises the aubergine (*Badhinjan*) as a 'unifier of taste' and a balanced remedy, suitable for both the elderly and the young, reflecting the scholarly tradition of viewing dietary choices as integral to spiritual and physical well-being.
